constraints: Algorithm A memory grows like N^theta, theta ~= 0.75
Table for O(1) rough-decision costs Theta(P_{<p}) = e^{(1+o(1))p} space
affordances: branchless wheel advancement vectorizes across streams (SIMD)

norms: ship Algorithm B for production when only primes are wanted
social.program: orthogonal stream prime generation research program (see paper.md, generator.md, min_factor.md, theory.md)

nodes.name: p-Rough Numbers
nodes.statement: The p-rough numbers R_p are the integers m >= 1 with gcd(m, P_{<p}) = 1, i.e. having no prime factor less than p.

sources.heading: 1. Notation
sources.quote: the p-rough numbers: no prime factor < p

nodes.name: Multiplier Set A_p
nodes.statement: A_p is the set of p-rough numbers from p upward, A_p = R_p intersect [p, infinity).

sources.heading: 0. TL;DR
sources.quote: A_p = \{a \ge p : \gcd (a, P_{<p}) = 1\}, the p-rough numbers from p up

nodes.name: Ownership Theorem
nodes.statement: For every prime p, the composites owned by p (those with smallest prime factor p) equal p times A_p, and the map a to pa is a bijection from A_p to Theta_p, with the family of Theta_p partitioning all composites.

sources.heading: 2.1 Ownership theorem
sources.quote: The map a \mapsto pa is a bijection A_p \to \Theta_p, and \{\Theta_p\}_p partitions the composites.

nodes.name: Proof of the Ownership Theorem
nodes.statement: Let m be composite with spf(m)=p and a=m/p; since m composite a>1 and every prime factor of a divides m so is >= p, giving gcd(a,P_{<p})=1 and a>=p; the converse and injectivity follow similarly, and every composite lies in exactly one Theta_{spf(m)}.

sources.heading: 2.1 Ownership theorem
sources.quote: Let m be composite with spf (m)=p and put a = m/p.

nodes.name: A_p is a Periodic Wheel
nodes.statement: A_p union {1} is periodic modulo P_{<p} with phi(P_{<p}) residues per period, is completely determined by its intersection with [1, P_{<p}], and is infinite.

sources.heading: 2.2 A_p is a wheel, not a prime list
sources.quote: A_p \cup \{1\} is periodic modulo P_{<p}

nodes.name: Phase Separation Lemma
nodes.statement: If a is in A_p and a < p^2, then a is prime.

sources.heading: 2.3 Phase separation
sources.quote: If a \in A_p and a < p^2, then a is prime.

nodes.name: A_p in [p,p^2) Equals Primes in that Range
nodes.statement: A_p intersected with [p, p^2) equals exactly the primes in that range; one period of A_p consists of 1 together with primes only iff P_{<p} <= p^2, which holds iff p <= 7.

sources.heading: 2.3 Phase separation
sources.quote: which holds iff p \le 7

nodes.name: First Composite Multiplier at p=11
nodes.statement: 121 = 11^2 is 11-rough and less than 210, so 121 is in A_11 and 11*121 = 1331 = 11^3 is owned by 11; among the 48 residues of one period there are 5 composite multipliers.

sources.heading: 2.3 Phase separation
sources.quote: First composite multiplier: 121 = 11^2 is 11-rough and <210

nodes.name: No Forward Dependency Corollary
nodes.statement: A_p is determined by primes strictly below p, all known once p is discovered; emitting composites up to n only needs multipliers up to n/p, so streams are consumed in increasing order and never stored as complete objects.

sources.heading: 2.3 Phase separation
sources.quote: Multipliers are consumed in increasing order, so the lists are streams, never stored objects.

nodes.name: NextOwnedComposite Primitive
nodes.statement: NextOwnedComposite(p,x) is the smallest composite owned by p that exceeds x.

sources.heading: 0. TL;DR
sources.quote: NextOwnedComposite reduces exactly to a rough-successor

nodes.name: NextOwnedComposite Reduces to NextRough
nodes.statement: NextOwnedComposite(p,x) equals p times NextRough(p, max(p-1, floor(x/p))), where NextRough(p,y) is the smallest element of R_p exceeding y.

sources.heading: 2.4 The primitive of generator.md, derived
sources.quote: the sought-after primitive is exactly a rough-successor

nodes.name: Prime Phase Advancement Lemma
nodes.statement: For a in A_p with a < p^2, NextRough(p,a) is the next prime after a (unless it exceeds p^2), so while the emitted composite is below p^3, advancing the stream of p is a single O(1) index increment into the prime array.

sources.heading: 2.5 Advancement inside a stream
sources.quote: advancing the stream of p is a single index increment into the prime array

nodes.name: Causality Theorem
nodes.statement: If all primes below n have been emitted and the scan reaches n = pa with multiplier a, then a <= n/2, the next multiplier a' = NextRough(p,a) satisfies a' < n, and a' is determined only by data about integers less than n.

sources.heading: 2.6 Causality: everything needed is already known
sources.quote: no step ever requires knowledge of an integer \ge n

nodes.name: No O(1) Time and O(1) State Primitive
nodes.statement: Deciding a in R_p is deciding gcd(a,P_{<p})=1; a branch-free O(1) decision with no auxiliary state must be a function of a mod P_{<p}, tabulating which costs Theta(P_{<p}) = e^{(1+o(1))p} space, while any stateless alternative amounts to trial division costing Theta(pi(p)); hence a fixed table serves only finitely many primes.
nodes.notes: Framed as a Remark with an accompanying informal proof sketch; treated as an obstruction result guiding algorithm design rather than a formally closed theorem.

sources.heading: 2.7 Why O(1) time and O(1) state per prime is not available
sources.quote: a fixed-size table can serve only finitely many primes

nodes.name: Min-Factor Normal Form
nodes.statement: Every n>1 is uniquely n = p^e r with p prime, e>=1, r in B_p (the monoid generated by primes greater than p); necessarily p = spf(n), e = v_p(n), r = n/p^e.
nodes.formal: n = p^{e} r,\ p=\mathrm{spf}(n),\ e=v_p(n),\ r=n/p^{e}

sources.heading: 2.8 The exponent refinement (min-factor normal form)
sources.quote: Every n>1 is uniquely n = p^{e} r

nodes.name: Cone Recursion
nodes.statement: B_p decomposes as {1} disjoint union over primes q>p of q times B_q; the multiplier cloud of p is generated by the clouds of the larger primes, with no residue system modulo P_{<=p} constructed.

sources.heading: 2.8 The exponent refinement (min-factor normal form)
sources.quote: The multiplier cloud of p is generated by the clouds of the larger primes

nodes.name: Strict Phase Separation Lemma
nodes.statement: If r in B_p and 1 < r < (p+1)^2 then r is prime, so a composite multiplier in layer (p,e) forces the emitted value to be at least p^(e+2), meaning layer e has a rough phase below N only for p <= N^{1/(e+2)}.

sources.heading: 2.8 The exponent refinement (min-factor normal form)
sources.quote: a composite multiplier in layer (p,e) forces the emitted value \ge p^{e+2}

nodes.name: Algorithm A: Exact One-Touch Orthogonal Generator
nodes.statement: Algorithm A recurses on the largest prime factor of each composite, splitting m=bq with b=m/P(m) and q=P(m), to create a stream tree Sigma_b of composites; each stream carries an emit cursor and a spawn cursor, giving a generator in which every composite up to N is touched exactly once with O(1) advancement, no marking array, and no divisibility test, at the cost of the number of live streams growing like N^theta with theta ~= 0.75.

sources.heading: 3. Algorithm A — exact one-touch orthogonal generator
sources.quote: each composite touched exactly once, O (1) advancement, no divisibility, no marking array

nodes.name: Stream Tree Theorem
nodes.statement: For b>=2 the stream Sigma_b of all b*q for primes q>=P(b) forms, over all b, a partition of the composites; each Sigma_b is increasing and its successor operation is a single index advance in the prime array.

sources.heading: 3.1 The idea: recurse on the multiplier, not on divisibility
sources.quote: {\Sigma_b}_{b\ge2} is a partition of the composites

nodes.name: Algorithm A Correctness Theorem
nodes.statement: A(N) emits precisely the primes at most N, in increasing order, and pops exactly one queue record per composite in [4,N].

sources.heading: 3.5 Correctness
sources.quote: A(N) emits precisely the primes \le N, in increasing order, and pops exactly one queue record per composite

nodes.name: Algorithm A Causality Theorem
nodes.statement: Every array access primes[j] performed while processing n in Algorithm A satisfies primes[j] < n, hence is always legal.

sources.heading: 3.5 Correctness
sources.quote: Every array access primes[j] ... satisfies primes[j] < n

nodes.name: Algorithm A Worked Trace at N=50
nodes.statement: A step-by-step trace of Algorithm A for N=50 shows all 34 composites in [4,50] consumed exactly once while the 15 primes are emitted.

sources.heading: 3.6 Worked trace (N = 50)
sources.quote: All 34 composites in [4,50] are consumed exactly once; the 15 primes are emitted.

nodes.name: Algorithm A Live Stream Count Bound
nodes.statement: A saddle-point estimate using Dickman's rho gives the number of live streams S(N) = N^{theta+o(1)} with theta approximately 0.75, which is sublinear but decisively worse than pi(sqrt N).

sources.heading: 3.7 Cost
sources.quote: gives S (N) = N^{\theta+o (1)} with \theta \approx 0.75

nodes.name: Algorithm A+Wheel Variant
nodes.statement: Combining Algorithm A with a fixed wheel modulus W removes smooth bases that dominate S(N) by requiring stream bases to be p_{w+1}-rough, empirically reducing live streams by roughly an order of magnitude at w=6 while preserving the one-touch property for all W-coprime composites.

sources.heading: 3.8 Variant A+wheel
sources.quote: the reduction is large (empirically an order of magnitude at w=6)

nodes.name: Algorithm B: Wheeled Streaming Generator
nodes.statement: Algorithm B fixes a wheel modulus W and relaxes the exact multiplier set A_p to the tabulated W-coprime relaxation for primes p>p_w, giving a genuine O(1) table-lookup advancement with O(1) state per prime, memory O(pi(sqrt N)+W), at the cost of duplicate touches (each surviving composite touched roughly omega_{>p_w} times instead of once).

sources.heading: 0. TL;DR
sources.quote: Algorithm B (§4) pays in duplicate touches

nodes.name: Algorithm B Coverage Lemma
nodes.statement: For every W-coprime composite m up to any bound, p=spf(m) exceeds p_w, a=m/p is W-coprime and a>=p, so m is a value of the stream of p under the relaxed multiplier set.

sources.heading: 4.4 Correctness
sources.quote: m is a value of the stream of p

nodes.name: Algorithm B No Early Claims Lemma
nodes.statement: Every key in Q during Algorithm B execution is at least n, and every key is a W-coprime composite at least p^2 for its owning prime.

sources.heading: 4.4 Correctness
sources.quote: Every key in Q is \ge n

nodes.name: Algorithm B Correctness Theorem
nodes.statement: B() emits exactly the primes, in increasing order, forever.

sources.heading: 4.4 Correctness
sources.quote: B() emits exactly the primes, in increasing order, forever.

nodes.name: Algorithm B State Theorem
nodes.statement: Advancement in Algorithm B uses no prime lookups at all, and activation uses primes[act] with primes[act]^2 <= n, so primes[act] < n; Algorithm B is a genuine online stream with O(1) state per prime.

sources.heading: 4.4 Correctness
sources.quote: Algorithm B is a genuine online stream with O (1) state per prime.

nodes.name: Algorithm B Duplicate Operations Bound
nodes.statement: The total queue operations for Algorithm B up to N approximate kappa_W * N * (ln ln sqrt N - ln ln p_w), which at w=6, N=10^12 gives approximately 0.46N ops versus the one-touch ideal of approximately 0.19N, roughly a factor 2.4 more touches in exchange for pi(sqrt N)=78498 records.

sources.heading: 4.5 Duplicate accounting (the honest cost of the relaxation)
sources.quote: Roughly a factor 2.4 more touches than Algorithm A

nodes.name: Algorithm C: Min-Factor Exponent-Spine Generator
nodes.statement: Algorithm C re-indexes Algorithm B by the min-factor normal form m=p^e r, streaming layers (p,e) instead of per-prime streams, so that every rejected candidate is reported as (spf, valuation, cofactor); it uses the wheeled relaxation of B_p (denoted tilde B_p), so it over-claims exactly as B does, and its touch count equals B's to within Theta(N^{2/3}/log N), meaning it is a streaming min-factor oracle, not a faster prime generator.

sources.heading: 0. TL;DR
sources.quote: It is a streaming min-factor oracle, not a faster prime generator.

nodes.name: Wheeled Relaxation of B_p
nodes.statement: The wheeled cloud tilde B_p that Algorithm C actually streams is {1} union {r>=p : gcd(r,W)=1, p does not divide r}, a W-coprime wheel that still contains composites, so it over-claims exactly as B does.

sources.heading: 4C.1 Design
sources.quote: \tilde B_p ... a W-coprime wheel that still contains composites

nodes.name: Algorithm C Coverage Lemma
nodes.statement: Every W-coprime composite m is a value of layer (p,e) with p=spf(m), e=v_p(m).

sources.heading: 4C.3 Correctness
sources.quote: Every W-coprime composite m is a value of layer (p,e)

nodes.name: Min-Factor Oracle Lemma
nodes.statement: The drained claimant with the smallest p in Algorithm C carries (spf(n), v_p(n), n/p^{v_p}); every claimant's p divides n hence is at least spf(n), and spf(n) claims by the coverage lemma.

sources.heading: 4C.3 Correctness
sources.quote: The drained claimant with the smallest p carries (\mathrm{spf} (n), v_p (n), n/p^{v_p})

nodes.name: Algorithm C Claimants and Duplicate Accounting
nodes.statement: The claimant set of Algorithm C for m is a subset of Algorithm B's claimant set, and the operation count for C equals that of B minus a discarded tail of size Theta(N^{2/3}/log N), so at N=10^12,w=6 the gap is about 10^{-4}N against ops_B ~ 0.46N, meaning Algorithm C is not a faster prime generator.

sources.heading: 4C.4 Duplicate accounting and cost
sources.quote: Algorithm C is not a faster prime generator.

nodes.name: Smallest Strict Witness at W=30 is 847
nodes.statement: At W=30, 847 = 7 * 11^2 is claimed twice by Algorithm B (via 7*121 and 11*77) and once by Algorithm C (layer (7,1), r=121), demonstrating the strict subset relation between claimant sets.

sources.heading: 4C.4 Duplicate accounting and cost
sources.quote: Smallest strict witness at W=30: 847 = 7\cdot11^2

nodes.name: Bucket Priority Queue Engineering Layer
nodes.statement: A segment length Delta is chosen and, for each future segment index s, a bucket list holds stream records whose next value lies in that segment; processing a segment drains its bucket with O(1) amortised operations sequential in memory, removing the log factor of a binary heap.

sources.heading: 5.1 Bucket priority queue (removes the log factor)
sources.quote: All operations are O (1) amortised and sequential in memory.

nodes.name: Numeric Hygiene Overflow Guard
nodes.statement: Guard every product before computing it by testing p > limit/a rather than p*a > limit, and use 128-bit or division form for N beyond 2^63.

sources.heading: 5.2 Numeric hygiene
sources.quote: Guard every product before computing it: test p > limit / a rather than p*a > limit.

nodes.name: Reference Implementation Validation Against Sieve of Eratosthenes
nodes.statement: The Python reference implementation validates Algorithms A, B and C by comparing their output at LIM=200000 against a reference sieve, asserting the one-touch property for A (pops equal composites) and checking Algorithm C's min-factor reports including the example 847 -> (7,1,121).

interfaces.note: no closed form fit performed, only assertion checks

sources.heading: 6. Reference implementation (Python, executable and self-checking)
sources.quote: assert st["pops"] == st["composites"], (st, "one-touch property violated")

nodes.name: Machine-Checkable One-Touch Assertion
nodes.statement: The assertion pops == composites in the reference implementation is the machine-checkable statement of exact orthogonality (Theorem 3.2), failing immediately if any composite is claimed twice or missed.

sources.heading: 6. Reference implementation
sources.quote: it fails immediately if any composite is claimed twice or missed

nodes.name: Comparison Table of Prime Generation Methods
nodes.statement: A comparison table lists touch/time cost, working memory, whether an array over the range is required, and segment-parallelism for trial division, segmented Eratosthenes, Pritchard wheel sieve, Atkin, O'Neill priority-queue sieve, and Algorithms A, B and C.

sources.heading: 7. Comparison
sources.quote: Algorithm A is the unique member of this table that touches each composite exactly once and uses no range-proportional array

nodes.name: idea.md (Wheels and Spectra)
nodes.statement: Both algorithms are structurally the wheel of idea.md section 2.3 made incremental: Algorithm B materializes the first w exclusion fields as a table and the rest as lazily-advanced pointers, avoiding the doubly-exponential primorial blow-up noted in idea.md section 8.5.

sources.heading: 8. Relation to the companion documents

nodes.name: fractal.md (Lattice Reading)
nodes.statement: The set deleted by the lattice recursion S_{k+1} = (p tilings of S_k) minus p*S_k is exactly Theta_p = p*A_p (Theorem 2.1); Algorithm A follows the recursion to full depth while Algorithm B truncates at depth w.

unresolved.description: Remark 2.9 is phrased as an informal obstruction argument ('Remark') but functions with the force of a theorem; classified as a conjecture/fuzzy-adjacent node at reduced confidence rather than as a theorem.
